- Changelog · Why a "},{"id":"p4s2","text":"plugin's settings go missing: the four-layer chain"},{"id":"p5s1","text":"## Why this one"},{"id":"p6s1","text":"- **No API key, eight engines.** AnySearch, CN Bing, DuckDuckGo HTML, www Bing, DuckDuckGo Lite and "},{"id":"p6s2","text":"360 Search are scraped directly; Exa joins the primary tier through its keyless MCP endpoint, and Fi"},{"id":"p6s3","text":"recrawl's search API is the measured fallback. - **Official release"},{"id":"p6s4","text":" facts, not generic ranking.** Explicit PostgreSQL, Rust and scoped npm queries start a narrow offic"},{"id":"p6s5","text":"ial lookup in parallel; `Rust 1.90 发布说明` returns the canonical Rust Blog announcement at rank 1. The"},{"id":"p6s6","text":" lookup is capped at 2.5 s and failure leaves the ordinary rows intact.
- **arXiv is a first-class r"},{"id":"p6s7","text":"esearch source.** An explicit arXiv paper or survey query is routed to arXiv's own API in parallel, "},{"id":"p6s8","text":"with boolean terms instead of a loose keyword string, so a survey query returns surveys rather than "},{"id":"p6s9","text":"incidental mentions. arXiv PDF links are read through the HTML full-text view instead of being rejec"},{"id":"p6s10","text":"ted as binary, and abstract pages parse even when a site-wide wrapper is named `footer`.
- **A tail "},{"id":"p6s11","text":"budget and an honest quota story.** Interactive searches release after two independent contributors "},{"id":"p6s12","text":"and cap at 5 s for Latin-script queries / 3 s for CJK queries. Firecrawl stays a fallback; `firecraw"},{"id":"p6s13","text":"lApiKey` is optional for users who need repeatable quota. Keyless Firecrawl cannot be made dependabl"},{"id":"p6s14","text":"e from the client side.
- **The ranking is measured, not asserted.** Cross-engine reciprocal-rank fu"},{"id":"p6s15","text":"sion with authority and freshness boosts, a 20-query offline benchmark, and an 81-configuration para"},{"id":"p6s16","text":"meter sweep — one of the few search plugins here that publishes its metric, per-query output and con"},{"id":"p6s17","text":"fidence intervals. See How the ranking works.
- **One package, two runtimes.** DSH gets the native p"},{"id":"p6s18","text":"lugin and one `web_tools` entry; Claude Code, Codex and other MCP clients get the same keyless searc"},{"id":"p6s19","text":"h through a dependency-free stdio server with `search`, `fetch`, `research` and `domain_search`. It connects two abiliti"},{"id":"p8s2","text":"es — looking things up and reading pages. What it finds can still be wrong or out of date, and the m"},{"id":"p8s3","text":"odel can still misread it. That is no different from searching the web yourself."},{"id":"p9s1","text":"### Large language models, and why they "don't know""},{"id":"p10s1","text":"A large language model — the kind of program behind ChatGPT or DeepSeek — is trained on an enormous "},{"id":"p10s2","text":"amount of text until it can predict the most likely next word. What it remembers stops at the moment"},{"id":"p10s3","text":" training ended; that moment is called the **knowledge cutoff**."},{"id":"p11s1","text":"It is not connected to the internet. Ask about yesterday and it does not "search and fail to find"; "},{"id":"p11s2","text":"it has **no route to that information at all**. Analogy: a scholar who has read the whole library bu"},{"id":"p11s3","text":"t moved to the mountains three years ago and stopped accepting parcels. Ask about three years ago an"},{"id":"p11s4","text":"d you get a solid answer. Ask about last week's news and you get inference dressed as fact."},{"id":"p12s1","text":"### Agents, and why they need tools"},{"id":"p13s1","text":"An agent is an AI that decides what to do next. A plain chatbot answers one question at a time. An a"},{"id":"p13s2","text":"gent thinks "should I look this up?", picks a tool, looks at the result, and then decides what to do"},{"id":"p13s3","text":""should I look this up?", picks a tool, looks at the result, and then decides what to do after that."},{"id":"p14s1","text":"A **tool** is a fixed capability handed to the agent: search, read a page, run a command. The model "},{"id":"p14s2","text":"cannot browse on its own, but it can ask the harness to run `web_search` with certain arguments. The"},{"id":"p14s3","text":" harness runs it, puts the result back into the conversation, and the model continues. Analogy: you "},{"id":"p14s4","text":"do not send the chef to the market; you give the chef a phone and let them call the buyer."},{"id":"p15s1","text":"## What it can do"},{"id":"p16s1","text":"Each line is the plain version first, the technical note second. The technical note is safe to skip."},{"id":"p17s1","text":"1. **Ask several search engines at once.**
[该节后续省略]"},{"id":"p18s1","text":"### Known limitations"},{"id":"p19s1","text":"- **Relevance is capped by upstream result pages** and is below a commercial search API. Key-free sc"},{"id":"p19s2","text":"raping gets throttled in return: measured, 360 served `访问异常页面` with a captcha and another domestic e"},{"id":"p19s3","text":"ngine a `x5sec` punish page. Such pages are now classified as `SEARCH_BLOCKED` instead of masqueradi"},{"id":"p19s4","text":"ng as zero results, and 360 is a fallback; cooldowns and multiple engines still only cover for it, n"},{"id":"p19s5","text":"ot all of it.
- **Google is unreachable from this network.** A tunnelled `www.google.com/search` ret"},{"id":"p19s6","text":"urns a JavaScript shell (94 KB, 1–3 links); headless Chrome is redirected to `google.com.hk` with a "},{"id":"p19s7","text":"reCAPTCHA. `gbv=1`, a consent cookie and a mobile user agent all failed. Eight public SearXNG instan"},{"id":"p19s8","text":"ces were unusable too (429/403/not JSON).
- **It depends on upstream HTML structure.** A redesign br"},{"id":"p19s9","text":"eaks a parser; that engine records a reason and yields to the next one rather than silently returnin"},{"id":"p19s10","text":"g nothing.
- **Titles, links and snippets only** — no page text. That is `web_fetch`'s job.
- **`web"},{"id":"p19s11","text":"_fetch` cannot resume a fetched page from an offset**: the host's `WebFetchRequest` carries only `ur"},{"id":"p19s12","text":"l`, so text beyond `fetchMaxLength` needs `read_page`, a higher limit or a narrower page.
- **`read_"},{"id":"p19s13","text":"page` keeps at most 2,000,000 characters per page**: anything beyond the cap is cut and flagged `tru"},{"id":"p19s14","text":"ncated`; the plugin caches at most eight bodies, so a ninth page evicts the least recently used one."},{"id":"p19s15","text":"
- **Extraction keeps only what looks like the article**: a page built entirely by JavaScript comes "},{"id":"p19s16","text":"back nearly empty by default; it is rendered only when you installed Playwright and enabled `renderJ"},{"id":"p19s17","text":"s`. Content outside the chosen article root — a sidebar table, say — is still dropped with the navig"},{"id":"p19s18","text":"ation.
- **Browser rendering has no measured real-page body**: the development environment for this "},{"id":"p19s19","text":"project has no Playwright. What is verified is shell detection, the silent fallback when no renderer"},{"id":"p19s20","text":" exists, and the render/timeout/fallback paths against an injected fake renderer (`render-js.test.ts"},{"id":"p19s21","text":"`). Rendered text from a real site is still unmeasured.
